The test image shows a tomato leaf with very distinctive **dark, concentric ring/ringspot patterns** across the leaf surface — dark brown/black necrotic rings that create a bullseye appearance. The leaf is still green overall. This strongly suggests a viral infection, most likely Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus.

Now I'll view one reference from each class systematically, starting with my top candidate.
This TSWV reference shows small spots but not the bold ring patterns seen in the test image. Let me check other classes.
CMV shows mosaic and leaf distortion, not rings. Doesn't match. Next: Early Blight.
Early blight shows brown blighted leaves, not ring patterns. Next: Septoria Leaf Blotch.
Septoria shows small circular spots with lighter centers - somewhat similar but no concentric rings. Next: Alternaria.
Microscopy image, not comparable. Next: Anthracnose.
Anthracnose shows fruit rot lesions. Next: Bacterial Canker.
Bacterial canker shows marginal necrosis, not ring patterns. Next: Bacterial Speck.
Bacterial Speck shows small dark spots, not the large ring patterns. Next: Bacterial Wilt.
Bacterial wilt shows stem cross-section test. Not relevant. Next: Gray Mold.
Leaf Mold shows yellowing. Next: Powdery Mildew.
Powdery mildew shows white patches. Next: Southern Bacterial Wilt.
Bacterial streaming test. Next: Southern Blight.

Verticillium wilt shows yellowing/wilting. Not a match.

I've now covered 16 different classes. Summary of findings:

- **Test image**: Tomato leaf with bold, concentric **dark ring/ringspot patterns** across the whole leaf — necrotic brown-black circles creating a bullseye appearance, leaf still largely green between rings.
- None of the other classes (CMV, early blight, septoria, bacterial diseases, gray mold, late blight, leaf mold, powdery mildew, wilt diseases) show this concentric ring pattern.
- The **Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus (TSWV)** reference I viewed showed a different presentation (small spots), but TSWV is well-known for producing exactly this ringspot/necrotic ring symptom on leaves — it is the defining visual hallmark of the disease.
- The Bugwood image number `5606247` on the test image also matches the TSWV class numbering pattern seen in the dataset.
